letter.title: Twenty-Five Years, Still You
paragraphs: I keep looking at that number and wondering how we got here so fast. August 29, 2001 feels like another lifetime, and at the same time, parts of it still feel like yesterday. We were younger, we had no idea what life was going to throw at us, and we definitely had no idea what the two of us were getting ourselves into. Especially me.

You poked my ass, I got embarrassed, you apparently decided I was worth keeping around, and somehow that ridiculous little beginning became twenty-five years of my life. And when I really think about that, there is one thing I keep coming back to: I am incredibly lucky.

I am lucky that out of all the people in this world, I found you. I am lucky that the woman I fell for all those years ago became the woman I got to build a life with. And I am lucky that after twenty-five years, I can still look beside me and see the same person who has been there through so many different versions of my life.

We were young together. We figured things out together. We made mistakes together. We struggled, adjusted, learned, grew older, and somehow kept building something that neither of us could have completely imagined when we started.

There are twenty-five years of memories between us now. Some are big enough that we will probably remember them forever. Some are so ordinary that we have already forgotten them. But I think those ordinary years are what I appreciate the most now. The meals. The drives. The errands. The trips. The conversations before going to sleep. The jokes nobody else would understand. The little routines that became part of our lives without us ever deciding they would.

The times you checked on me. The times you worried about me. The times you pushed me when I needed pushing. The times you took care of things without ever asking for credit. There are probably hundreds of things you have done for me and for our family that I never thanked you for properly.

So on our twenty-fifth anniversary, I want you to know something that I probably do not say enough: I see it. I see how much you give. I see how much you care. I see how fiercely you love me. I see the things you carry quietly and the things you do because somebody has to do them. And I appreciate you more than I know how to put into words.

You have been beside me through some of the best moments of my life, but what means even more is that you were beside me when life wasn't particularly exciting or easy. You were there during the years when we were simply trying to figure things out. You were there while I was becoming the person I am now. And whether you realize it or not, a very large part of that person exists because of you.

You challenged me. You expected more from me. Sometimes you probably expected more from me when I was perfectly happy giving less. And yes, that occasionally annoyed the hell out of me. But twenty-five years later, I can admit something. Most of the time, you are right. Please do not frame that sentence. You already have enough evidence to use against me.

But seriously, Baby, you have made me want to be better. A better husband. A better partner. A better man. Not because you demanded perfection from me, but because loving you made me care about the kind of person standing beside you.

I also hope you understand how loved you are. Not just because you are my wife. Not because twenty-five years says I am supposed to love you. Not because we have history. I love you because after all this time, I still genuinely like the person you are.

It gives me joy seeing you laugh. I see your beautiful face. I still notice that little pout. And you still have the habit of biting your lip for no reason. And yes, I am still amazed that this gorgeous, sexy woman somehow ended up being my Baby.
Twenty-five years have passed, but you have never become ordinary to me. Familiar, yes. Comfortable, definitely. Occasionally irritating? Absolutely. But never ordinary.

There is something very different about loving someone when you are young and loving that same person after you have watched years pass together. When we were younger, I loved you for who you were. Now I love you for who you were, who you became, what we survived, what we created, and for all the pieces of our lives that are tied together because we chose to stay beside each other.

I know twenty-five years has not always been easy. There were moments when we were tired. Moments when we misunderstood each other. Moments when one of us probably wanted to throw the other one out of the house. Maybe both of us.

But when I look back now, I do not measure our twenty-five years by the difficult moments. I measure them by everything that came after them. We continued. We grew. We laughed again. We planned something else. We made another memory. We woke up the next day and continued being us. That means more to me now than I could have understood twenty-five years ago.

If somebody had shown the younger me our life today, I probably would not have believed them. I would not have understood how much life two people could fit inside twenty-five years. And I definitely would not have understood how lucky I was about to become. Because meeting you did not just give me someone to love. It gave me a partner. A family. A history. A person who knows where I came from, knows who I am now, and knows most of the embarrassing parts in between.

You have seen me succeed. You have seen me fail. You have seen me confident and completely unsure of myself. You have probably seen versions of me nobody else ever will. And somehow, you are still here. That is something I will never take lightly.

So this anniversary, more than anything else, I want to say thank you. Thank you for the twenty-five years you gave me. Thank you for every sacrifice I noticed and every one I probably didn't. Thank you for worrying about me. Thank you for taking care of me. Thank you for believing in me. Thank you for calling me out when I deserved it. Thank you for laughing at my stupid jokes. Thank you for making our life feel like ours. And thank you for still reaching for me after all these years.

We are older now. Definitely older. I would say wiser too, but I don't want to exaggerate on such an important occasion. There is more gray hair, more aches in places that never used to hurt, and probably a lot more conversations beginning with, “Do you remember where I put...?”

But I wouldn't trade where we are now for where we were then. Because now I know you in a way I couldn't have known you at the beginning. Now there are twenty-five years behind every time I say, “I love you.” Twenty-five years of proof. Twenty-five years of memories. Twenty-five years of us.

And somehow, I still feel like there is more ahead of us than I am ready to miss. I want the next trips. The next ridiculous projects. The next quiet mornings. The next family memories. The next stupid argument we won't remember a week later. The next year. And the one after that.

I don't know exactly what the next twenty-five years will look like. But if I am lucky enough to have them, there is nobody else I would rather grow old with. And yes, Baby, we are growing old. Together. Which means I’m gonna keep whining about it.

I hope you know how important you are to me. I hope you know how appreciated you are. I hope you know that I do not look at these twenty-five years and think about how much time has passed. I look at them and think about how fortunate I am that I got to spend that time with you. Of all the things that could have happened with my life, somehow, I got you. That is still one of the best things that have ever happened to me.
Happy 25th anniversary, my Baby. Thank you for my past. Thank you for my present. And thank you for still being the person I want beside me for whatever comes next.
I love you, Bodin. More knowingly than I did twenty-five years ago. More gratefully. More completely. And still with enough immaturity left in me to remind you how all of this started.
So yes... If I could go back to August 29, 2001, knowing exactly what the next twenty-five years would bring, I would still choose you. I would just keep one eye on you whenever you walked behind me.

birthdayLetter.title: A Letter to My Baby Bodin
paragraphs: Almost 25 years together... and somehow you are still my favorite person to argue with about absolutely nothing.

I honestly thought by now we'd be calm, mature adults who handle disagreements with wisdom and grace. Instead, we still debate like it's a competitive sport. Bu I guess we both both are just very passionate. We have Olympic-level stamina for teasing each other, misunderstanding each other, and then laughing about it five minutes later.
You drive me crazy. And somehow, that is still one of my favorite places to be.

You are demanding - yes, you are. You always want to be treated like a baby. You want to be taken care of. You want attention. You want cuddles. You want reassurance. You want to feel assurance every single day. You want to feel chosen every single day.
And the truth is... I love that about you.
I love that you want all of that from me. It annoys me like crazy. But it also makes me feel so special. It makes me feel like the most important person in the world to you.
Because it means I am your safe place. It means I'm the one you trust to hold you when you're tired. It means I'm the one you expect to show up.
And I always have and I will always be there..
You are gorgeous. Not just "pretty." Not just "cute." Gorgeous.

For almost 25 years, I still look at you and think, "How did I get this hot, sexy woman to choose me?" The way you smile. The way you laugh when I tell the worst corny joke. The way you look at me when you're annoyed but still secretly entertained. The way you pout when your lips form that little expression that says, "You better fix this."

You are stunning. Yes, physically - that part is undeniable and unfairly impressive for me even though you don't agree. I don't care!- but even more in the way you carry yourself. Your determination. Your standards. The way you protect what's yours. The way you fight for our family like a viking warrior.
You demand the best from me - even when I don't want to give it. And because of you, I grow. Because of you, I try harder. Because of you, I am not the same man I was 25 years ago.

You make me better. Even when your lips are pouting at me about something small. Even when you're giving me that look that says I messed up. Even when you're refolding the clothes that I already folded.
You sharpen me. You steady me. You challenge me.
And you love me.

Thank you for loving me. The stubborn one. The immature one. The quiet one. The loud one. The one who pretends he doesn't care but cares deeply. The version of me that was still figuring life out. The version that made mistakes. The version that didn't always say the right thing.
Through all of it... you stayed.
You chose me. Again and again. Not just on easy days - but on the complicated ones. On the tired ones. On the "we're not talking right now" ones.
That kind of love isn't luck.
That's commitment. That's loyalty. That's real.
If I had to start over - if I had to relive every argument, every blanket stealing battle, every snoring war, every cleanliness inspection and memory lapse disagreement - I would still pick you.
Every time.
Not because we're perfect.
But because we're us.
And behind all the sarcasm and teasing, here's the truth I don't joke about:
You are my home. You are my comfort. You are my fire. You are my peace. You are my chaos and my calm. You are my baby.
And after 25 years, I don't love you out of habit.
I love you with intention.
I love you because I see you. I know you. And I choose you.
For as long as I breathe, I will keep choosing you - on the loud days, on the quiet days, on the annoying days, on the passionate days.
Even if you steal the blankets first.
I love you. Happy Valentine's Day, Baby.
